entries.title: The same blue draws the data and marks the phrase
entries.summary: Chart lines move from ink to pen, the family blue, and a phrase here and there gets a hand-drawn underline in that same blue. Two on the page, no more.

options.title: Pen for the line, gold at the end
options.blurb: The series is drawn in the family blue; the one gold dot still marks where it lands, which is the single annotation the house viz rule allows per chart.
options.picked: Keeps the annotation reading as an annotation instead of competing with a blue line.

options.title: Underline as a mark, not a style
options.blurb: The underline is a stretched SVG of two pen passes, so no two are the same length and none of them is a text-decoration rule. Used on the thing a reader would repeat, not on every claim.

entries.title: A shelf, not a sermon
entries.summary: First page up: a scroll of five posts, two kinds of proof. The name has a swear in it, so the first screen has to read as a gift rather than a rant.
entries.note: I kind of feel like something needs to go up before Saturday. To fulfill my role, my commitment to myself.

options.title: The scroll
options.blurb: Name, one promise line, posts newest first. Five posts and the page is real; adding one is appending a block.
options.picked: Smallest honest page, and it leaves the chart-first version available later with no rework.

options.title: Manifesto over stream
options.blurb: Three or four paragraphs on what the site is for, then the stream. Rejected: the words have to be JC's, and a manifesto written for him is exactly the rant a stranger already expects.

options.title: Chart as the front door
options.blurb: One long-run chart fills the first screen. Strongest first impression, but it fixes the register as a data site before anything has been posted in the other three types. Held as the next move.
